key_insight: Combining computational simulation and neural networks identified a favorable HDPE friction stir welding window at 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: Bottom preheating can reduce plunge loads and thermal gradients, supporting more stable welding and fewer void defects in HDPE joints.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defect formation.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force responses.
Combined simulation and neural-network predictions to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Predictive performance is established within the tested parameter space; extrapolation to other conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
